summary.text: A 78-year-old woman with known Osler-Rendu-Weber disease, including multiple episodes of epistaxis from nasal and cutaneous telangiectasia, presented with abdominal pain, asthenia and weight loss. Colonoscopy showed sigma diverticulosis and serum CA19.9 was elevated above 1000 KU/l. CT identified a 25 mm hilar lesion invading the fourth segment with intrahepatic bile duct dilation, vascular invasion, hepatic telangiectasia, ectasia of the celiac trunk and hepatic artery, and a 15 mm intrahepatic aneurysm.

CT-guided biopsy showed a carcinoma with biliary immunophenotype. Multidisciplinary discussion rated surgical risk extremely high, so cisplatine-gemcitabine chemotherapy was given for only two cycles before suspension for pulmonary embolism, and rivaroxaban was introduced. Surgery was then reconsidered: liver function was normal, CA19.9 was 40 KU/l, and a new discussion judged surgery the best option given local disease extension without extrahepatic disease.

The 3D CT reconstruction confirmed the preoperative findings and future remnant liver volume was 41% of total liver volume, considered adequate. Angiography showed hyperinflux with hepatic telangiectasia, and before surgery the intrahepatic aneurysm was embolized with metal spirals with an uneventful post-procedural course. A left extended hepatectomy with caudate lobe and bile duct resection, lymphadenectomy and bilioenteric anastomosis was then performed, with 570 min operating time and 500 cc blood loss.

A CT scan at post-operative day 7 showed no abdominal collection or other complications and regular remnant liver vascularization. The postoperative course was uneventful with a 10-day hospital stay, no ascitic decompensation and no postoperative bleeding. Pathology showed a 25 mm suprahilar small-duct mucinous cholangiocarcinoma, R0 resection, six negative lymph nodes and ypT4N0, with liver changes compatible with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. The patient was disease free after 12 months follow up.
